PullRequest.Title: agentHost: update bundled Codex SDK to 0.153.0
PullRequest.Body:
Updates bundled `@openai/codex` from `0.149.1` to `0.153.0`, regenerates the app-server protocol, and includes the guardian/test compatibility fixes.

Replaces #335474 under my account for normal team-member review. The automation-produced branch and head commit are unchanged: `9805e0f253c0cf75e885e3cfbc3d8c904c71fd04`. The original PR preserves the updater and repair history.

Validation on this commit:
- All 89 non-policy GitHub checks passed, including Compile & Hygiene.
- [Product build 472857](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=472857&view=results): platform, publishing, and sanity-test stages passed. Overall status is `partiallySucceeded` because Copilot NOTICE generation failed. Release was disabled.

Authenticated Codex Agent Host launch remains a manual sign-off.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added branch, unbounded string type, and call path are explicit: `summarizeGuardianReviewAction` feeds `formatGuardianDenialNotification`/`formatGuardianReviewStatusNotification`; the denial path emits a durable `ChatResponsePart` and two tool-card actions; the state reducer retains both response and invocation text; `ProtocolServerHandler` broadcasts each envelope. Only the prevalence and typical size of large interactive stdin payloads is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: String bytes and allocations in Markdown formatting, AHP protocol payload bytes, retained chat/replay objects, and rendered Markdown nodes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(n) in the unbounded stdin length for formatting and retention, and broadcast serialization scales further with the number of connected relevant clients; one denial emits the large content in a durable Markdown action and again through tool-call actions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Synchronous CPU/GC pressure and UI rendering latency, with retained chat memory proportional to the stdin payload.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the protocol union and summary switch had no `writeStdin` action, so terminal-input payloads were not copied into durable Markdown or approval-card messages by this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Denied, timed-out, or aborted write-to-stdin reviews now surface the complete stdin payload as UI detail. `_handleGuardianReviewCompleted` synchronously formats that detail into Markdown and also sends it as both the tool-call intention and invocation message.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `case 'writeStdin'` at line 157 assigns the entire unbounded `action.stdin` string to the display `detail`; the preceding SDK type diff adds `writeStdin` to `GuardianApprovalReviewAction`, so this is a newly reachable path.
Findings.Title: Bound stdin before copying it into review UI state
Findings.Impact: If an agent sends a large script, generated data, or other bulk content to an interactive process and guardian denies or times out the write, the agent-host performs synchronous full-input scans/copies and the workbench receives and renders the entire payload. This can stall the review UI, increase IPC cost, and retain substantial duplicate text in chat/replay state.
Findings.Evidence: `GuardianApprovalReviewAction` newly permits `{ type: 'writeStdin', stdin: string }` with no size limit. At line 157 the full string becomes `summary.detail`. `formatGuardianDenialNotification` then calls `trim`, scans all text with `/`+/g`, interpolates another full Markdown string, and prefixes every line. `_handleGuardianReviewCompleted` stores that Markdown as a durable response part and reuses the raw detail in `ChatToolCallStart` and `ChatToolCallReady`; each action is dispatched into chat state and broadcast over the AHP transport. Thus one denied large stdin write creates multiple O(n) strings, protocol payloads, retained state entries, and a large Markdown render.
Findings.Recommendation: Create a bounded, escaped preview for the `writeStdin` summary (with a truncation indicator) before it reaches Markdown/tool-card state, while keeping the original `params.action.stdin` only for the exact `approveGuardianDeniedAction` round-trip.

Scenarios.Scenario: Surfacing and optionally overriding a denied/timed-out write-to-stdin guardian review
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On an `item/guardianApprovalReview/completed` notification, summarization, Markdown construction, state reduction, and AHP broadcast all occur synchronously before the denial/status is visible. The reverse request to Codex is off this initial display path and occurs only after the user approves anyway.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receives the newly supported writeStdin guardian action from the Codex app-server JSON-RPC stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound app-server notification per distinct review; duplicate IDs are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Codex 0.149.1 and the generated action union did not expose the writeStdin review variant.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcasts chat response/tool actions carrying the raw or formatted stdin text over AHP.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three display envelopes for a denied review (durable Markdown, tool-call start, and tool-call ready), sent to each relevant connected client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existing broadcast path did not receive writeStdin-derived display payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transfers the full stdin-derived text to UI clients and triggers live state updates/rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes the full original guardian event to `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request for the review when the user selects accept or accept-for-session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No writeStdin event could be round-tripped by this adapter; other guardian action kinds already used the same single request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on initial review rendering; it gates applying the user's override.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective input is one deduplicated guardian review, with cost proportional to `action.stdin` length and secondarily to the number of relevant connected UI clients.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each distinct review notification is handled independently; duplicate review IDs are suppressed. A denial emits one durable response action plus tool-call start/ready actions serially, and each envelope is synchronously broadcast to every relevant connected client.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in rendering a guardian review. `handledGuardianReviews` deduplicates by review ID, but the complete display payload is retained in chat state; the protocol replay buffer also keeps up to 1,000 recent envelopes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added branch forwards the entire string, downstream formatters perform full-string scans/copies, reducers retain it, and protocol code broadcasts it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical writeStdin payloads may be short, but the protocol type imposes no bound and interactive processes can receive large scripts or generated data. This uncertainty limits severity to medium; it does not affect the established linear work and retention mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the new variant copies unbounded stdin into durable Markdown and approval-card state, causing linear synchronous allocation, IPC, retention, and rendering work. The display can be safely bounded without changing the exact approval round-trip.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm Codex agent-host startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold agent-host launch resolves the bundled Codex executable and starts one app-server subprocess. Warm session operations reuse that connection. The changed manifests select version 0.153.0 but do not alter launch scheduling in repository code.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Starts the platform-specific bundled Codex app-server binary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess launch per cold Codex connection; reused while warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same launch path and cardinality used Codex 0.149.1; the diff only changes the pinned binary version to 0.153.0.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The app-server must become ready before Codex sessions can progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cold connection versus reuse on warm sessions; no collection-sized fan-out was added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One app-server child process is started for the active Codex connection; existing connection generation/reuse behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The app-server process is reused once connected; no changed cache key, negative cache, or prewarm policy is evidenced by the dependency metadata update.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that repository-level launch cardinality and scheduling are unchanged; no claim is made about opaque binary internals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Binary-internal startup cost and package size are not observable from the supplied source diff, so no performance regression can be established from the version number alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the dependency version changes the executable contents but provides no diff evidence of extra startup work, process fan-out, or cache defeat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal Codex protocol request and notification processing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Protocol declarations affect build/type-check compatibility, not runtime message processing after erasure. Runtime requests still serialize once to the existing app-server stdin and notifications still arrive on its stdout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes JSON-RPC messages and writes them to the Codex subprocess.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One JSON serialization/stdin write per existing client request and one parse/dispatch per incoming message; method cardinality is caller-controlled and unchanged by the type regeneration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical client transport behavior existed before; regenerated unions only describe additional fields and methods.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing subprocess IPC operations remain on request/event critical paths, but the declarations add no executable work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Build-time declaration count grows modestly; runtime cost does not scale with the 827 generated declaration-file changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing JSON-RPC request concurrency and notification dispatch are unchanged by the generated type-only declarations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Generated protocol files contain TypeScript type declarations and type-only imports/exports; they create no runtime cache. Existing request correlation and event mapping behavior remains in handwritten code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository search found only type exports/imports in the generated protocol tree, so these changes are erased at runtime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The SDK binary may internally implement new methods, but generated type declarations alone do not establish execution frequency or cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: generated protocol changes are type-only and do not themselves add runtime serialization, IPC, I/O, or retained objects.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the 840-file inventory. Most changes are generated type-only protocol updates plus dependency pins and test fixture adjustments. One medium-severity serialization/rendering regression was submitted for copying unbounded writeStdin content into durable UI state and multiple protocol actions; no other diff-backed runtime performance regression or regression fix was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
